name: dayOfWeek
column17: notes
Low incline 15-30 deg. Bar to collarbone, no excessive arch, elbows below 90 deg for a max upper-chest stretch. Ramp up: empty bar then 3-4 low-rep warm-up sets, never 10 reps near working weight.
Chest-supported only so the lower back stays fresh for Tuesday. Full protraction at the bottom.
Flat press without leg drive; feet in the air or relaxed. 1-2 s pause on the chest.
Super-wide pronated. Dead hang at the bottom with a slight pause, chin over the bar.
Seated anterior delt press: bench one notch below 90 deg, shoulder-width grip, bar to collarbone. Stop short of absolute failure to protect the shoulders.
Squeeze in the shortened position after the stretch-biased presses.
Chest-expander pull-apart equivalent: underhand grip, rear delts and mid traps.
Half the load of a normal lateral raise; full arc overhead for scapular rotation and shoulder health.
Light second weekly arm stimulus without a deep tendon stretch so the elbows stay fresh for Saturday.
Full depth below parallel, heels elevated (lifting shoes or plates) for more knee flexion and quads. Do not grind to RPE 10. Ramp: 2 x 10 empty bar, 135 x 10, 225 x 5, then triples.
Hips back, torso to ~45 deg, never parallel to the floor. Keep reps in reserve; builds titan erectors.
Weighted sissy squat (or leg extension): the reliable way to load rectus femoris in the stretch. Hold a support.
Direct knee flexion, controlled lowering.
Full range: legs to the bar with a posterior pelvic tilt, no swinging.
Deep stretch on a block or in a belt squat machine.
Optional if the machine is available. Light, far from failure: spinal decompression and blood flow.
Weighted dips, leaning forward with a deep stretch. Chest high, controlled tempo, protract at the top.
Bent forward at the bottom; 45 lb plates limit the last inches of the squeeze and load the stretch.
Heavy quad and glute work without loading a tired lower back. Leg press or Bulgarian split squat also work.
Controlled lowering, no explosive jumps. Focus on lateral delts and scapular mobility.
Straight arms across a bench, hips low in the arc. Breathe in on the way down, strong exhale with a stomach vacuum on the way up.
Straight after the pullover, which pre-stretches the abdominal wall.
Heavy stretch then explosive pull for upper and mid traps. Farmer walks 30 m are an alternative.
Full range, no jerking. Build a base before any advanced neck work.
Dual-rope pushdowns before heavy extensions: lubricates the elbows. Elbows slightly back at lockout for the long head.
Main biceps mass builder. Strict lowering, no hip swing. Long-term target 135 lb for reps.
Builds lockout strength and mass around the elbow and the lateral/medial heads. Barbell or Smith.
Long head of the biceps in a stretch. 60 deg preacher curl is an alternative that blocks cheating.
Pinwheel hammer curls across the body with Fat Gripz: brachioradialis and upper forearm.
Fat-grip wrist curls, forearms on a bench. Goal: match your one-arm dumbbell curl load (at least 40 lb per hand).
Weighted AbMat or decline sit-ups, plate on the chest or behind the head. Progress towards 45 lb (~20 kg) through a full spine range.
Neck flexion for front/side symmetry. Optional: finish with planks 3 x 60 s as a last superset.
Optional finisher: arm-biased weighted chin-ups, only if your elbows are 100% fresh.

High local leg stimulus without spinal load. Split squat with a higher deficit is an alternative.
Bent-over barbell row with a lifting belt or a board on the bar to standardise the stretch (cuts the heaviest top inch).

Heavier progression: add load gradually in the 15-20 rep range.
